items.title: SoftBank reports $7.1bn quarterly loss including $3.7bn U.S. AI data-center equipment charges
items.summary: SoftBank reported a roughly ¥1.12 trillion quarterly loss, including $3.7 billion in charges on prepaid U.S. data-center power equipment after project changes. Its Tokyo shares fell as much as 10.5% on November 11, but recovered to close down 0.44%. The result highlights financing and execution pressure rather than a demonstrated collapse in AI compute demand.

items.title: UKMTO Warning 201-26 reports distinct November 10 tanker projectile strike near Lima, Oman
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 201-26 records a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman, on November 10 at 13:38 UTC. The master reported the crew safe and no environmental impact, with damage inspection deferred until first light. The vessel, attacker and incremental oil-throughput impact remain unverified; this is distinct from November 7 tanker incidents.

items.title: TSMC October revenue jumps 59.7%; board approves $40.93 billion capacity appropriations
items.summary: TSMC reported record October revenue of NT$586.89 billion, up 59.7% year over year and 14.7% from September. Its board approved $40.93 billion in capital appropriations and up to $500 million each for investments in Anthropic and OpenAI. The approvals are not evidence that funds have been spent or equity purchases closed.

items.title: CoreWeave Q3 revenue jumps 168% and backlog reaches $132.5 billion
items.summary: CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion of Q3 revenue, up 168% year over year, beating estimates, and raised full-year guidance to $13.0–$13.3 billion. Shares rose more than 7% in November 10 extended trading after a severe monthly decline. Its $132.5 billion backlog supports demand visibility, while debt and spending create significant execution risk.

items.title: Reported drone strike causes fire at Russia's Ust-Luga export port
items.summary: Russia's Leningrad governor reported a drone strike and fire at Ust-Luga port, three injured workers and a local power disruption. Ust-Luga handles oil and petroleum-product exports, but the damaged terminal and export-flow impact remain unverified. This is a leading infrastructure-risk signal rather than a confirmed crude-supply outage.
